runs: Worked example A: an outage delayed by authority

A hypothetical network operations incident, not an account of any employer. A fiber cut causes an outage. Repair waits because the escalation matrix routes approval through non-technical executives, two of whom are in conflict.
locate the break, verify alarms, arrange access, estimate repair time.
rebuild the timeline. When was the diagnosis available, which authorization was missing, and what evidence supports the claim of obstruction?
why does rank rather than technical competence control dispatch, and who can change that rule?

Map customers, field crews, carrier partners, technicians and executives, keeping responsibility, expertise and control separate. A technician who cannot safely challenge a manager is part of the model, not a personality defect. “Fast escalation” as a measure can reward notifying executives while repairs wait.

Split diagnosis-to-dispatch from dispatch-to-restoration. The first is organizational delay; the second is mostly physical repair. This split is the most directly testable idea in the practice, and regulator investigations of outages often carry timelines detailed enough to apply it.
